question: What is the typical maximum volume of medication given in one subcutaneous site?
explanation: Subcutaneous tissue can only accommodate small volumes of medication without causing distension and pain. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is medication absorption slower in the subcutaneous layer than in muscle tissue?

options.A: The pH of fat is very acidic
options.B: Enzymes in fat destroy the drug quickly
options.C: The needle used is much thinner
options.D: Fat tissue has a poor blood supply

explanation: Adipose tissue is less vascular than skeletal muscle, leading to a slower and more gradual rate of drug uptake. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h1)

question: Another name commonly used for the subcutaneous layer is what?
explanation: The hypodermis is the anatomical layer situated immediately below the dermis containing fat and connective tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h2)

question: A patient with very little body fat requires what adjustment during a subcutaneous injection?

options.A: Pushing the medication in twice as fast
options.B: Giving the injection directly into the muscle
options.D: Using a shorter needle or a 45-degree angle

explanation: Thin patients lack thick fat layers, meaning a standard 90-degree angle with a long needle risks hitting muscle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the recommended distance to keep away from the umbilicus when giving an injection in the abdomen?
explanation: Staying two inches away from the umbilicus avoids the highly vascular and sensitive periumbilical area. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is regular site rotation critical for patients receiving daily subcutaneous injections?

options.A: It prevents the needle from becoming blunt
options.B: It prevents lipohypertrophy and tissue damage
options.C: It stops the skin from changing colour permanently
options.D: It ensures the medication reaches the bloodstream faster

explanation: Repeatedly using the same spot causes fatty lumps or tissue breakdown, which disrupts normal drug absorption. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which needle gauge is most typical for a standard adult subcutaneous injection?
explanation: A 25 to 27 gauge needle is thin enough to minimize pain while still allowing viscous fluids to pass through. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main reason nurses avoid recapping used injection needles?

options.A: It wastes valuable time during medication rounds
options.B: It causes the needle tip to become contaminated
options.C: It increases the risk of accidental needle stick injuries
options.D: It makes the syringe difficult to dispose of safely

explanation: Trying to recap a used needle frequently leads to accidental punctures, transmitting bloodborne pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h4)

question: At what angle should a standard subcutaneous needle be inserted into a patient with average adipose tissue?
explanation: The correct insertion angle depends on needle length and skin fold size, typically falling between 45 and 90 degrees. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is the skin allowed to dry completely after cleaning with an alcohol swab?

options.A: Wet alcohol makes the skin too slippery to pinch
options.B: Alcohol must dry to destroy microorganisms effectively and prevent stinging
options.C: Dry skin ensures the needle slides in without bending
options.D: Moisture interferes with the adhesive properties of plasters

explanation: Letting the antiseptic dry allows chemical disinfection to take place and stops burning pain as the needle enters. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the medical term for the thickening or pitting of subcutaneous fat caused by repeated insulin injections?
explanation: Lipodystrophy describes abnormal fat tissue changes resulting from failure to rotate injection sites properly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h6)

question: A patient develops a small bruise immediately after a subcutaneous injection of heparin. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Apply a hot water bottle to dissolve the hematoma
options.B: Massage the area vigorously to disperse the pooled blood
options.C: Notify the physician immediately to stop all heparin doses
options.D: Apply firm, gentle pressure to the site without rubbing

explanation: Applying gentle pressure stops bleeding, but rubbing must be avoided especially with anticoagulants to prevent worsening the hematoma. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h6)
